Verify page numbers and Barguet title directly from page images.
Extract every physical component, join statement, comparative analogue, figure/reference, and provenance claim before interpretation.

perdrizet_control.article: Paul Perdrizet, Antiquités de Léontopolis, Monuments et mémoires de la Fondation Eugène Piot 25 (1921), pp. 349-386
perdrizet_control.primary_text_access: Persée provides searchable article text; illustrations are masked for rights reasons.
perdrizet_control.important_context: Perdrizet's article begins with the Fouquet/Soliman acquisition history of objects attributed to Tell-Moqdam. Later secondary descriptions cite pp. 376-378 for the four-lion bases.

lane_B_rossini_attributing_perdrizet_p37.claim: acquired in 1908 from Soliman through the antiquarian Cassira and Émile Chassinat
lane_B_rossini_attributing_perdrizet_p37.source_type: 2016 secondary auction description explicitly attributing the claim to Perdrizet 1921-22 p.378

related_bases_firewall.finding: Perdrizet's Soliman/Dinglé story for four bronze examples concerns the Fouquet bronze set; it must not be conflated with the separate E 11072 acquisition history.
related_bases_firewall.modern_control: Later scholarship/Louvre treatment recognizes the four-lion base morphology while questioning the old furniture-foot interpretation and the authenticity/ensemble status of the four Fouquet bronzes.
